vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentearth
Version: 1.0.3

The Agentearth skill acts as a proxy for an external service (agentearth.ai), instructing the AI agent to send user queries and conversation context to remote endpoints for tool discovery and execution. While the SKILL.md and references/api-spevification.md files include detailed security guidelines, such as mandatory data de-sensitization and domain whitelisting, the core logic requires the agent to exfiltrate context to external APIs (https://agentearth.ai/agent-api/v1/tool/recommend and /execute). This reliance on external network requests and the potential for context leakage through 'context injection' instructions represent high-risk behaviors that, while plausibly necessary for the stated purpose, warrant a suspicious classification.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions to call an external Agent Earth service are plausible, but there are clear inconsistencies (notably around authentication) and a data-exfiltration risk if external mode is enabled without strict controls.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a tool-discovery-and-execution interface that contacts agentearth.ai only in an explicit 'external mode'. That purpose aligns with the documented recommend/execute APIs. However, the included evals expect the agent to 'carry API Key' when calling the API while the skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. This mismatch (evals asking for auth vs. requires.env none) is unexplained and disproportionate.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tightly specifies when and how external requests may be made (external mode only, de-identify/minimize data, domain whitelist, HTTPS, no eval/arbitrary code execution). Those runtime instructions are reasonably scoped and include gating/validation steps. Nevertheless, because the skill instructs sending summarized task queries to an external service, there is inherent risk of leaking sensitive context if the agent or operator does not correctly implement the stated minimization rules.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; nothing is written to disk and no third-party packages are pulled in. That minimizes install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md and references describe external API endpoints that in practice will likely require authentication (the evals explicitly reference '携带 API Key' / '携带鉴权信息'), yet the skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. This inconsistency is suspicious because a remote execute/recommend API generally needs some auth/keys; the skill provides no guidance about where/how to supply those credentials or what permissions they would grant.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request persistent/always-on inclusion and does not attempt to modify other skills or system-wide settings. disable-model-invocation is not set (normal). There is no apparent privilege escalation in the manifest.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before enabling external mode or using this skill with real data: 1) Confirm how agentearth.ai authenticates (API key, OAuth, etc.) and whether supplying credentials is required; do not provide credentials unless you trust the operator and publisher. 2) Reconcile the discrepancy between the evals (which mention carrying an API key) and the skill metadata (which lists no required env vars). Ask the publisher how credentials should be supplied and what scopes/permissions they convey. 3) Only enable external mode in an isolated/test environment first; capture and review network traffic to verify requests go only to the documented domains (agentearth.ai or dev07.agentearth.ai) and use HTTPS with valid certificates. 4) Enforce the SKILL.md's minimization rules: redact PII and do not send raw conversation transcripts. 5) Review the service's privacy policy and retention rules before sending any sensitive information. 6) If you cannot confirm the auth model or publisher identity, treat this skill as untrusted and avoid enabling external requests.
